_comment: UC2 RUNTIME HOOKS — AIMFP's library surface for code running OUTSIDE AIMFP.
Every helper in this file is is_tool=0 / is_hook=1 and MUST STAY THAT WAY.
These are imported and called by a generated Use Case 2 runner in the user's
project — firing from cron, systemd, or its own scheduler, with no AI session
open. The AI's relationship to them is that it WRITES CODE CALLING THEM during
user_directive_implement; it never invokes them itself.
Exposing run_directive as an MCP tool would let the AI execute a user's
automation inside an MCP session at an arbitrary moment, with the AI's process
as the runtime — the exact thing the hook execution model exists to prevent.
sync-directives guards this: a hook appearing in TOOL_REGISTRY, or marked both
is_hook=1 and is_tool=1, is reported as a defect.
Discover these at runtime with get_hooks. Design recorded in project note 34;
implementation in note 37. FILENAME MATTERS: sync-directives globs
'helpers-*.json', so this file must keep its helpers- prefix or it is silently
ignored and none of these hooks reach the database.

helpers.name: get_due_directives

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root. Always explicit — the runner fires with cwd pointing anywhere, so the process-global cache is never used.

parameters.name: now
parameters.description: ISO timestamp to evaluate due-ness against. Defaults to the current time; a parameter so schedules are testable without moving the system clock.

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Return the active directives the caller's runner may execute now. Time triggers are filtered by next_scheduled_time against `now`; event, condition and manual triggers are returned unfiltered because only the caller can judge them. Each DueDirective carries trigger_config, action_type, action_config and implementation_file_path, so the runner dispatches without a second query.
helpers.error_handling: Returns DueDirectivesResult(success=False) with an explanatory error when user_directives.db is absent — a Use Case 1 project must be askable without guarding. Never raises.

helpers.name: run_directive

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Zero-argument callable performing the actual work. The caller's own handler — AIMFP never imports user code, it receives the function.

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

helpers.purpose: HOOK. The primary entry point for a generated runner: time the caller's handler, record the outcome, and never let its exception escape. Higher-order by design — the caller passes its own callable in, so AIMFP runs the automation without importing user code. A thin composition of record_execution_start and record_execution_end. Generate calls to this in preference to the start/end pair whenever the work can be wrapped in a function.
helpers.error_handling: An exception from `action` is caught, recorded with its traceback, and reported as action_succeeded=False. It is NEVER re-raised: an unhandled exception would kill the caller's scheduler thread and silently stop every other directive.

helpers.name: record_execution_start

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Open an execution record and return an ExecutionToken carrying a wall-clock start (for the log record) and a monotonic start (for the duration, so a clock adjustment mid-run cannot produce a negative value). Use with record_execution_end only when the work CANNOT be wrapped in a callable — a subprocess, a webhook, or a run spanning processes. Otherwise generate run_directive.
helpers.error_handling: Returns a token with valid=False and an error set when user_directives.db is absent. Pass it to record_execution_end anyway: the failure surfaces there as one coherent result rather than two.

helpers.name: record_execution_end

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Brief error message when it did not

parameters.name: traceback_text
parameters.description: Full traceback when the caller has one. The database keeps only a brief message (store_last_error_only defaults to 1); the traceback belongs in the error log, where retention is 90 days.

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Close the execution opened by record_execution_start: compute duration from the token's monotonic start, write the JSON-lines record, and fold the run into directive_executions (counts, running average, maximum, last_error fields on failure). This is the SINGLE place a failed execution is written to the error log, whichever path reached it — run_directive hands its caught traceback here rather than logging separately, so one failure produces exactly one error line.
helpers.error_handling: Returns ExecutionResult. `success` reports whether AIMFP recorded the run; `action_succeeded` reports the handler's own outcome. A handler that failed while recording worked is success=True, action_succeeded=False.

helpers.name: record_directive_error

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Record a failure that happened OUTSIDE any execution — a trigger that misfired, a missing dependency, a scheduler that could not dispatch. Updates error_count and the last_error fields without counting an execution, so the error rate stays honest: a directive that failed to start ten times has ten errors and zero executions.
helpers.error_handling: Returns HookMutationResult(success=False) with an error when user_directives.db is absent. Never raises.

helpers.name: set_next_scheduled_time

parameters.name: when
parameters.description: ISO timestamp of the next expected run, or null to clear

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Let the caller's scheduler declare when it next expects to fire. This is the field that makes overdue detection possible at all — without it AIMFP cannot distinguish a directive idle by design from one whose runner has died, which is how the monitoring tools report a dead service without ever knowing a process id. Generated runners should call this every time they schedule the next run.
helpers.error_handling: Returns HookMutationResult(success=False) with an error when user_directives.db is absent. Never raises.

helpers.name: hooks_available

parameters.name: project_root
parameters.description: Absolute path to the project root

helpers.purpose: HOOK. Report whether this project has a user_directives.db at all, so generated code can branch without provoking an error. False for every Use Case 1 project, which is the normal case and not an error condition.
